answer: Bonded stake makes sybils expensive: each agent identity must lock collateral, priced like a crystal lens—clear, costly to forge. An attacker spawning a thousand fake agents to flood rewards loses a thousand bonds the moment proof-of-work slips, yet gains only marginal reward share. Rational attackers abandon the attack when bonded cost exceeds expected loot. Equilibrium: few honest agents, one bond each, ocean of noise recedes to a dune of signal.
